conventions.field: F_2[t]/(t^19+t^5+t^2+t+1), 19-bit integers, bit j = coefficient of t^j
conventions.column_order: all multilinear monomials of degree <= D sorted by (-degree, bitmask ascending) (= the ann-v1 coordinate order)
conventions.macaulay_rows: (mu, k), mu over multilinear monomials of degree <= D-2 by degree ascending then ascending sorted index tuple, row index mu_index*19 + k, zero rows retained
conventions.dims_by_deg: dim(X cap B_{<=d}) for d = 0..4 (d = 0..3 for nothing else); counted as echelon rows with leading monomial of degree <= d in the graded column order
conventions.one_in_X: the constant polynomial lies in the F_2-subspace X
conventions.W_iteration: dims_W_i lists dim W^(0), ..., dim W^(i*+1) with i* = fixpoint_index = the first i with dim W^(i+1) = dim W^(i); one_first_iteration = first i with 1 in W^(i) (0 = already in rowspace(M_4)), null if never
conventions.E_hex: E_layout of the specification: 19 hex integers (no 0x prefix), bit j (LSB first) = column j of mu_order(2, 20)
conventions.hex_format: lowercase hexadecimal digits without a 0x prefix (int(s, 16))
conventions.wdag_mu: sorted list of variable indices, [] for the constant monomial

elimination_method: Own C kernel (code/gf2kern.c), bit-packed incremental semi-echelon basis: every row has a distinct leading column (its first set coordinate in the degree-descending column order) and a vector is reduced by XOR-ing the row of its lowest set pivot coordinate until no pivot coordinate is set; a nonzero remainder is appended. Rank = number of rows; dims_by_deg from leading degrees; '1 in X' iff the constant column (last) is a pivot. The certificate checkers (code/checkers.py) use a separate numpy Gauss-Jordan elimination and float32 BLAS parity products and share no code with the kernel.

detail.selection: random stream; systems with literal final_dim > 18 skipped (brute force enumerates 2^dim elements); after the first 12 comparisons, only fixpoint-index >= 2 systems are taken until three exist

construction.method: generic expansion of S_3(x_1, x_2, x_R) over F_{2^19} (algebra.descend_S3)

ambiguities.clause: EXP-CERTBIN-4e92d7 object.macaulay_matrix (columns in DESCENDING degrevlex, constant LAST) and EXP-CERTBIN-e94b27 object.mutant_closure_W_D ('a basis of W^(i) intersected with B_{<=D-1} is the set of RREF rows (descending degrevlex columns) whose leading monomial has degree <= D-1')
ambiguities.chosen: Every matrix and closure uses the degree-graded order (-degree, bitmask ascending), which is the ann-v1 coordinate order; the basis of W^(i) cap B_{<=3} is the set of semi-echelon rows whose leading monomial has degree <= 3.
ambiguities.why: BR-1: column order and pivot rule do not affect ranks, subspace dimensions or membership of 1. For any degree-graded order the echelon rows with leading degree <= d span X cap B_{<=d}, and W^(i+1) depends only on the span of the multiplied basis, so every recorded quantity is order-independent. The constant monomial is last in both orders.

ambiguities.clause: Q3 'the list dim W^(0), dim W^(1), ... up to the fixpoint; the fixpoint index' and e94b27 'stop at the first i with dim W^(i+1) = dim W^(i)'
readings_considered: the list ends with the confirming computation W^(i*+1)
ambiguities.chosen: dims_W_i = [dim W^(0), ..., dim W^(i*), dim W^(i*+1)] (last two equal); fixpoint_index = i* = the first i with dim W^(i+1) = dim W^(i); one_first_iteration = the first i with 1 in W^(i), 0 meaning 1 in rowspace(M_4), null if never; final_dim = dim W^(i*).
ambiguities.why: Records every computed iteration (BR-4 'record dim W^(i) for every i'); i* matches the specification's own usage ('fixpoint at iteration 0' for W_4 = M_4; 'iterations_to_fixpoint 1' for final dim 4427 > 3819).

ambiguities.clause: W iteration continues after 1 enters W^(i)
readings_considered: iterate to the dimension fixpoint as literally stated
ambiguities.chosen: Iterate to the dimension fixpoint (literal rule); one_first_iteration records when 1 first appeared.
ambiguities.why: BR-4 states the stopping rule as the first i with dim W^(i+1) = dim W^(i) and asks for the final dimension and dims_by_deg(W_4).

ambiguities.clause: BR-3 route 2: 'for each x_1 in V, solve S_3(x_1, x_2, x_R) = 0 for x_2 in F_{2^19}'
ambiguities.chosen: S_3 = (x_1 + x_R)^2 x_2^2 + x_1 x_R x_2 + x_1^2 x_R^2 + B as a polynomial in x_2 with a = (x_1+x_R)^2, b = x_1 x_R, c = x_1^2 x_R^2 + B. a,b != 0: x_2 = (b/a) z with z^2 + z = ca/b^2, solvable iff Tr = 0, z by the half-trace; b = 0, a != 0: the unique square root of c/a; a = 0, b != 0: x_2 = c/b; a = b = 0: every x_2 if c = 0 (all 1024 elements of V counted), none otherwise. Every root is re-checked by direct evaluation of S_3; roots in V are those < 1024.
ambiguities.why: Exact case analysis; the degenerate sub-cases (x_1 = 0, x_1 = x_R) occur for every input (x_1 = 0 is in V), so they must be handled rather than excluded.

ambiguities.clause: certificate_format: 'each a hex integer' (L_hex) and E_layout 'E_hex is a list of 19 hex integers'
ambiguities.chosen: Lowercase hexadecimal digits without a 0x prefix, stored as JSON strings (int(s, 16) parses both forms).
ambiguities.why: JSON has no hex literal; the encoding is recorded in rederivation.json conventions.

ambiguities.chosen: mu is the ascending list of its variable indices ([] for the constant monomial), as in blind-inputs.json monomial_encoding; node ids are 0..N-1 in list order and every child id is smaller than its parent's.
ambiguities.why: Matches the input encoding; the checker nevertheless sorts nodes by id and enforces (a) literally.

ambiguities.clause: ell_and_rc_b step (1) and BR-5 (blind reading fixed by the card)
ambiguities.chosen: Kernel dim 1: its nonzero vector. Kernel dim > 1: the lowest unit vector e_k in the kernel (row k with no quadratic part) if any, with the dimension recorded; otherwise 'not applicable (kernel dim d)'. Kernel dim 0: 'not applicable (kernel dim 0)'. The quadratic-column submatrix is the 19 x 190 block of the E_layout columns 21..210 (all degree-2 monomials), for curve and explicit inputs alike.
ambiguities.why: As fixed by BR-5; dim 0 is the only case BR-5 does not name and has no vector to use.

ambiguities.clause: ell_and_rc_b step (3) ('No substitution') and the fields of Q4
ambiguities.chosen: When ell's linear part is zero the step-3 label is recorded, j* and every R'_3 / R'_4 / sigma / T5 field is null, and ell_route is still computed with ell = 0 or 1.
ambiguities.why: Step (3) forbids the substitution; ell_route is defined for any ell.

ambiguities.clause: derived_per_instance 'for S_3 and N-CONV19: ell_route' vs BR-5 'SEPARATELY, compute ell_route DIRECTLY'
readings_considered: every input for which step (1) yields an ell
ambiguities.chosen: Every input for which step (1) yields an ell (curve and explicit kinds).
ambiguities.why: The arm of an explicit input is blind to this task; computing it everywhere loses nothing and the comparator may select.

ambiguities.clause: BR-5 'For curve-kind inputs also check c_k = Tr(t^k / x_R^2)'
ambiguities.chosen: Recorded as a boolean for curve-kind inputs with x_R != 0 and rc_b step (1) giving a vector; null for explicit inputs and for x_R = 0 (1/x_R^2 undefined).
ambiguities.why: The formula is undefined at x_R = 0 and meaningless without x_R.

ambiguities.chosen: The span of ell * m for all 1351 multilinear monomials m of degree <= 3 in v_0..v_19, each product multilinearly reduced (degree <= 4).
ambiguities.why: B_{<=3} is the span of those monomials.

ambiguities.clause: Q7_optional 'for curve-kind systems where rc_b applies'
ambiguities.chosen: W'_4 (literal W rule, 19 variables, 19 substituted equations) is computed wherever the rc_b substitution was applied, for both kinds; required_by_card marks the curve-kind ones.
ambiguities.why: Extra records cost nothing and are labelled.

ambiguities.clause: BR-7 ('SEAL BEFORE YOU WRITE ANYTHING ELSE ... Only then write report.yaml') vs BR-10 ('write a skeleton report first and fill it system by system')
readings_considered: per-system checkpoint files as the skeleton; report.yaml only after the seal
ambiguities.chosen: The system-by-system skeleton is checkpoints/ (one JSON per system, a progress log, the self-test record) plus logs/; report.yaml and attestation.yaml are written only after seal.txt.
ambiguities.why: BR-7 is explicit about the order of report.yaml; the checkpoints satisfy BR-10's continuation purpose without violating it. code/ necessarily precedes the seal.

ambiguities.clause: BR-2 'your literal W_D against a brute-force fixpoint'
readings_considered: brute force = hold W as the set of all its elements
ambiguities.chosen: Brute force holds each W^(i) as the set of ALL its elements and multiplies EVERY element of degree <= D-1 (feasible for dim <= 18); an additional independent Python-integer elimination covers larger and refuted 6-variable systems.
ambiguities.why: Enumerating all elements is the least structured computation of the literal rule; the second check extends coverage.

ambiguities.clause: dims_by_deg for spaces in 19 variables (R'_4, W'_4)
ambiguities.chosen: dim(X cap B'_{<=d}) for d = 0..4 over the 19 relabelled variables.

ambiguities.clause: wdag-v1 construction for refutations first reached at iteration L
ambiguities.chosen: Collapse per variable: 1 = sum(M_4 rows) + sum_j v_j a_j with a_j in W^(L-1) cap B_{<=3}; each a_j is one node expressed the same way one level down (levels rebuilt as rowspace(M_4) + span{v_j b : b in a basis of the previous level cap B_{<=3}}, whose dims are asserted equal to the literal iteration's); level 0 nodes carry M_4 rows only.
ambiguities.why: Construction is free (BR-6); validity is decided only by the checker.
